Paul Atreides is one of the most fascinating characters in science fiction, and his story in Frank Herbert’s Dune novels is far more complicated than a traditional hero’s journey.

First introduced in Dune (1965), Paul is a young nobleman born into a world of political rivalries, ancient traditions, and powerful religious beliefs. As his story unfolds, he begins to understand the enormous responsibility that comes with power.

Frank Herbert never wanted readers to blindly admire powerful leaders. Through Paul, he explored the dangers of hero worship, the influence of religion, and how easily people can place their faith in someone they believe is destined for greatness.

Denis Villeneuve brings this complexity to the screen beautifully, with Timothée Chalamet portraying Paul’s gradual transformation through both Dune (2021) and Dune: Part Two (2024).

And for anyone who loves the films, Herbert’s books offer an even deeper understanding of Paul Atreides and the extraordinary world surrounding him.
